case_name: State Of Uttaranchal v Alok Sharma & Ors
facts: The State of Uttaranchal v Alok Sharma & Ors
Supreme Court of India
15 April 2009
Civil.Appeal.
Two government companies being M/s. Teletronix Ltd. and Kumaon Television Ltd. were the subsidiary companies of Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam Ltd.
The employees of the said government companies were retrenched.
The State of Uttar Pradesh took a policy decision to appoint the employees of the said government companies.

For the said purpose, it framed rules purported to be in exercise of its power under the proviso appended to Article 309 of the Constitution of India, known as the Uttar Pradesh Absorption of Retrenched Employees of Government of Public Corporations in Government Services Rules, 1991 (for short "the Rules").
The term 'retrenched employee' is defined in Rule 2(c) of the Rules as under:
The charging provision is contained in Rule 3(1) of the Rules, which reads as under:

Admittedly, except Karan Pal, respondent No. 1 in Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) No. 6451 of 2005 who was appointed in the month of January, 1980 and Vijay Kumar Joshi, respondent No. 1 in Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) No. 8239 of 2005 who was appointed on 1.07.1983 (they were absorbed in the services of the State on 14.12.2005), other respondents herein were appointed after the cut-off date provided for in the Rules, viz., 1.10.1986.

It also does not appear that pursuant to or in furtherance of the provisions contained in Rule 3(1) of the Rules, the State Government has issued any notified order requiring absorption of retrenched employees in any post or service under the Government or prescribed any procedure therefor including relaxation in various terms and conditions of recruitment in relation to the retrenched employees
The State of Uttar Pradesh, however, issued a letter to the Managing Director of Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam Ltd on 30.12.1995.
While informing that approval has been granted by the Governor for winding up of the aforementioned companies, it was stated:
It is contended that in terms of paragraph 3 of the said circular letter, no such order had been issued by the Personnel Department of the State of Uttar Pradesh.

However, it appears that the Secretary to the Government of Uttar Pradesh issued a letter addressed to all Principal Secretaries / Secretaries of the Government of Uttar Pradesh, all Heads of the Departments and all Commissioners, Uttar Pradesh stating that on humanitarian ground a decision has been taken by the State for adjustment of the employees/ officers retrenched from the said units, subject to the terms and conditions laid down therein; some of which are inter alia being:
The said orders were issued with the consultation and approval of the Personnel Department.

As despite framing of the aforementioned rules and issuance of the aforementioned circulars, respondents had not been absorbed in the services of the State, they filed writ applications before the High Court of Uttaranchal.

The case of Vijay Kumar Joshi, respondent No. 1 in the Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) No. 8239 of 2005 was decided first wherein having regard to the fact that he was appointed prior to the cut-off date, his writ petition was allowed by an order dated 03.11.2004.
Following the said judgment, other writ petitions were also allowed by an order dated 6.06.2005, noticing:
Intra-court appeals preferred there against were dismissed by the High Court opining that this Court had issued limited notice in the special leave petitions filed there against.
It was held:

Ms. Pinki Anand, learned Addl. Advocate General appearing on behalf of the State, would submit that the respondents herein having not fulfilled the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars dated 30.12.1995 and 26.02.1996 as they were appointed after the cut-off date, and as they had not been working continuously and furthermore as no notification was issued by the Personnel Department, the impugned judgments cannot be sustained.

It was furthermore contended that in terms of the Rules, notified orders were required to be issued and the said condition having not been complied with, the Rules could not be said to have come into force.

Statutory rules, it was urged, could not have been superseded, modified or altered by reason of executive instructions as the procedures laid down for making a rule were required to be followed therefor.
issues: Interpretation and/or application of various circular letters issued by the State of Uttar Pradesh which have been adopted by the State of Uttarakhand after it was formed in terms of the U.P. State Reorganisation Act is in question in these appeals.
Whether the respondents, who were appointed after the cut-off date provided for in the Rules, are entitled to be absorbed in the services of the State?
Whether the State has fulfilled the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars dated 30.12.1995 and 26.02.1996?
Whether the impugned judgments can be sustained in view of the non-compliance with the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars?
Whether the Rules could have been superseded, modified or altered by reason of executive instructions as the procedures laid down for making a rule were required to be followed therefor.
petitioner_arguments: The respondents, who were appointed after the cut-off date provided for in the Rules, are entitled to be absorbed in the services of the State.
The State has fulfilled the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars dated 30.12.1995 and 26.02.1996.
The impugned judgments can be sustained in view of the non-compliance with the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars.
The Rules could not have been superseded, modified or altered by reason of executive instructions as the procedures laid down for making a rule were required to be followed therefor.
respondent_arguments: The respondents, who were appointed after the cut-off date provided for in the Rules, are not entitled to be absorbed in the services of the State.
The State has not fulfilled the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars dated 30.12.1995 and 26.02.1996.
The impugned judgments cannot be sustained in view of the non-compliance with the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars.
The Rules could have been superseded, modified or altered by reason of executive instructions as the procedures laid down for making a rule were required to be followed therefor.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the respondents, who were appointed after the cut-off date provided for in the Rules, are entitled to be absorbed in the services of the State.
The Court also held that the State has fulfilled the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars dated 30.12.1995 and 26.02.1996.
The Court further held that the impugned judgments can be sustained in view of the non-compliance with the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars.

The Court also held that the Rules could not have been superseded, modified or altered by reason of executive instructions as the procedures laid down for making a rule were required to be followed therefor.
holding: The final decision is that the respondents, who were appointed after the cut-off date provided for in the Rules, are entitled to be absorbed in the services of the State.
The Court also held that the State has fulfilled the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars dated 30.12.1995 and 26.02.1996.
The impugned judgments can be sustained in view of the non-compliance with the conditions precedent for application of the said circulars.
The Rules could not have been superseded, modified or altered by reason of executive instructions as the procedures laid down for making a rule were required to be followed therefor.
